value.name: declines weekend work
value.description: She decides not to stay late on Friday and not to work over the weekend on the Serrano matter, except by thinking about it.
evidence: would not stay late on a Friday and she would not work over the weekend on the Serrano matter except to think about it

value.name: reflects on apartment attachment
value.description: The narration explains that she has stayed in her small Pine Street apartment for years because she never looked for a better place and has grown attached to its afternoon light.
evidence: She lived in a small apartment on Pine Street that she had rented seven years ago intending to stay one year, and which she had stayed in because she had never gotten around to looking for somewhere better and because the light in the front room in the late afternoon was a light she had become attached to in a way she had not become attached to many things.

value.name: makes dinner and reads
value.description: She makes dinner and reads for an hour at home.
evidence: She made dinner. She read for an hour.

value.name: sleeps badly and wakes early
value.description: She sleeps poorly, wakes at four, and lies awake thinking about the curtain rather than the codicil.
evidence: She slept badly and woke at four and lay for some time looking at the ceiling and thinking not about the codicil but about the curtain.

value.name: notices curtain movement
value.description: She recalls that the curtain had moved, an observation that unsettles her and suggests she felt watched.
evidence: with a feeling of being seen

value.name: rationalizes curtain movement
value.description: She explains the curtain's movement as a normal draft caused by someone walking past the window and treats her reaction as tired misperception.
evidence: She had decided, on Thursday evening, that it had moved because Lucia, or possibly Rosa, had walked past the window inside the sewing room, and that the movement of air a person creates by walking past a curtained window is enough to stir the curtain, and that this was a perfectly ordinary mechanical fact about curtains and the bodies of people and the rooms of old houses, and that her noticing it as she had noticed it, with a feeling of being seen, was the kind of perceptual error a tired professional makes at the end of a hard week, and that the appropriate response to such an error was to file it and forget it.

value.name: fails to forget curtain
value.description: Although she mentally files the incident away, she does not actually forget it.
evidence: She had filed it. She had not forgotten it.

value.name: wakes and makes coffee
value.description: She gets up at five-thirty and makes coffee.
evidence: She got up at five-thirty and made coffee.
